source_text: Soranus of Ephesus, a prominent physician active around 98–138 CE, detailed the procedure in his Gynaecology, advocating excision of the protruding portion of an oversized clitoris using a scalpel after cauterization to prevent hemorrhage, specifically to mitigate friction-induced discomfort or nymphomania-like symptoms.
